Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #408
Title: Config/Settings dump?

What's the best way to dump all of the settings using starlette.config? I want to create an endpoint to make it easy to review the settings being used but I don't want the Secrets to be viewable, e.g. things like:

    JWT_SECRET = config("JWT_SECRET", cast=starlette.datastructures.Secret)

We are currently using:

```
@router.get("/settings", tags=["Info"])
def get_settings() -> dict:
    dctconfig = dict(settings.config)
    return dctconfig
```
But it shows the the secrets (instead of Secret('**********')) along with everything else.

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #408
Title: Config/Settings dump?

You can’t use `settings.config` directly, since it’s just a view onto the environment- it doesn’t “know” about how you’ve cast each element in it. We might want to think about debug level logging for any config accesses.

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #542
Title: issue with graphene dependency and starlette[full] installation

This week we discovered that would couldn't build our startlette application due to a very strange depenency error with `anisio8601`.  We are doing a full install of starlette 0.12.0 (`starlette[full]`). After using `pipdeptree` to track things down, I discovered that, `graphene` a startlette dependency has a dependency on `aniso8601`. 

`pipdeptree` show me the following

```
Warning!!! Possibly conflicting dependencies found:
* relativetimebuilder==2.0.0
 - aniso8601 [required: >=7.0.0,<8.0.0, installed: 5.1.0]
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Warning!! Cyclic dependencies found:
* aniso8601 => relativetimebuilder => aniso8601
* relativetimebuilder => aniso8601 => relativetimebuilder
```

graphene requires `aniso8601==5.1.0` and then there is some weird circular dependency as you see above.  

My solution, for now, which is not ideal, is to install starlette with minimal dependencies and then add only the ones that I am using `itsdangerouse` and `python-multipart`.

Anyway, let me know what you think.

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #542
Title: issue with graphene dependency and starlette[full] installation

Okay, thanks for highlighting this.
Not sure there's anything really we can do from our side here, right?

I guess another workaround in the meantime would be to have a *pinned* version of `graphene==2.1.4` in your dependencies, along with `starlette[full]`.

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #542
Title: issue with graphene dependency and starlette[full] installation

See https://github.com/graphql-python/graphene/issues/1008

The Graphene team is planning on releasing `v2.1.6` to fix this.

Issue: #619
Title: GraphQL support should be a third party application.

How easy would it be to replace the existing solution with any of the suggested alternatives? It looks like the current solution is quite strongly coupled to graphene, or am I wrong? 

The idea would be to output the schema as plain text or json to a third party library?

I would gladly see even over-simplified example to appear in the documentation because its not clear to me how everything is interacting. For example I can see in strawberry's case that:

I found an example in Ariadne's documentation: [Starlette integration](https://ariadnegraphql.org/docs/0.4.0/starlette-integration) where they use the string version of the schema (aka `type_defs`). There is a discussion about this [here](https://github.com/mirumee/ariadne/issues/115).

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #383
Title: Incorrect redirect location

If you call `url_path_for` on an application, you'll get the URL path for the application's routing.
Note that it *could* also be submounted in more than one location.

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #383
Title: Incorrect redirect location

sub_app.py
```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse

sub_app = Starlette()


@sub_app.route("/method1")
def http_method1(request):
    return RedirectResponse(sub_app.url_path_for('http_method2'))

@sub_app.route("/method2")
def http_method2(request):
    return PlainTextResponse("method2")
```

main.py:
```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette

from sub_app import sub_app

app = Starlette()

app.mount("/sub_app", sub_app)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host='0.0.0.0', port=8000)

```

Expecting that `/sub_app/method1` will redirect to `/sub_app/method2`. In fact in it redirects to `/method2` which is incorrect.

Reason of that, is `sub_app.url_path_for('http_method2')` returns `/method2`. Looks like sub_app does not know, that it is mounted via `/sub_app`

Issue: #814
Title: How to use request.url_for in mounted apps

I'm trying to compose apps from smaller Starlette apps. I can't find a way to make mounted apps that work regardless of app that is mounting them when using url_for.

In code below the mounted app can't use its *internal* names. It has to be somehow made aware that it's now running under namespace set by root app. Otherwise route cannot be found. With correct name hierarchy reversing URL does work.

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse
from starlette.routing import Route, Mount

async def sub(request):
    return PlainTextResponse(f"Subpage {request.url_for('sub')}") # doesn't work
#  return PlainTextResponse(f"Subpage {request.url_for('under:sub')}") # works

subroutes = [
    Route("/", endpoint=sub, name="sub")
]

subapp = Starlette(routes=subroutes)

async def homepage(request):
    return PlainTextResponse("Homepage")

routes = [
    Mount("/under", subapp, name="under"),
    Route("/", endpoint=homepage, name="root")
]

app = Starlette(routes=routes)
```

Repository: encode/starlette
Issue: #814
Title: How to use request.url_for in mounted apps

I've contributed a fix in #1416 that tries first to look up routes in the _local_ app, and then fails back to the global router.

So with this fix both 
```
return PlainTextResponse(f"Subpage {request.url_for('sub')}") # didn't work, fix in #1416
```
```
return PlainTextResponse(f"Subpage {request.url_for('under:sub')}") # still works
```

will return the correct url.

> I'm mounting another ASGI application via `mount` but it always redirects from `/another` to `/another/`. I've found a similar issue with sub-routers (#414) which was solved.
> 
> ### Example
> ```python
> from fastapi import FastAPI
> 
> app = FastAPI()
> 
> another_app = FastAPI()
> 
> 
> @another_app.get("")
> def root():
>     return "alive"
> 
> app.mount("/another", another_app)
> ```
> 
> ### Description
> I'm using `httpie` for this example.
> 
> ```
> $ http localhost:8000/another
> HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
> Transfer-Encoding: chunked
> date: Mon, 04 Jan 2021 08:40:02 GMT
> location: http://localhost:8000/another/
> server: uvicorn
> ```
> 
> As you can see, a redirect to `/another/` is happening.
> I'm just using another `FastAPI` app as example here.
> In my real world use-case the other application is the `GraphQL` ASGI app from the Ariadne GraphQL framework.
> The behavior is the same. I've also verified that the redirect is triggered by FastAPI by setting a breakpoint in the `GraphQL` ASGI app which wasn't hit.
> In the particular use-case shown above it's not even possible to hit the registered URL since it's registered on `""` instead of `"/"`. This doesn't apply to my real world use-case but I could imagine that there are other ASGI apps which don't respond on `"/"` but on `""` only which couldn't be mounted in FastAPI at all due to this.
> I realize that probably all ASGI apps register their root routes on `"/"` and not `""` so probably everything is working by design here but in my case I'm getting a lot of redirects from `/graphql` to `/graphql/` now which actually crashes the client app which doesn't handle redirects for security reasons.
> 
> ### Environment
> * OS: [e.g. Linux / Windows / macOS]: macOS
> * FastAPI Version [e.g. 0.3.0]: 0.63.0
> * Python version: 3.8

As disgusting as this might seem, the following might be a temporary solution:

 ### Example
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

if app.router:
   app.router.redirect_slashes = False
```

The only downside with this temporary solution, is all this same behaviour will be applied to all the routes in the app
